h1: 7 Shop Vacs That Also Blow Leaves and Dust, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Wet-Dry Vacuums With Blower: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 wet-dry shop vacuums that double as blowers, compared on tank size, peak horsepower, filters and use, from garage to job site.
summary: The DEWALT 9 Gallon DXV09PA is the one to buy if you want a shop vac with an actual blower function and attachments, built for heavy and frequent work. The DEWALT DXV04T is the compact job-site version, the Stanley 6 Gallon is the budget blower, and the Vacmaster and Amazon Basics suit garages and smaller jobs.
intro: Peak horsepower is the number every shop vac box leads with, and it is the one number that tells you almost nothing. It describes the motor under a lab condition no hose ever sees. What decides whether a blower function is useful is airflow and the shape of the exhaust port, which is why a 2 peak HP unit can clear a garage floor while a bigger number sulks. Buy on tank size, hose and attachments, and treat the horsepower as marketing.

This ranking looks at seven wet-dry vacuums that advertise or support a blower mode. We reviewed each from its listing, comparing tank capacity, the stated peak horsepower, filter design, attachments and the job each is meant for. Where a listing is quiet on blower details, we say so, and we tell you to confirm the exhaust port before you buy.

products.name: DEWALT 9 Gallon Wet/Dry VAC, Heavy-Duty Shop Vacuum with Attachments, 5 Peak HP, with Blower Function, DXV09PA
products.verdict: A 9 gallon, 5 peak HP shop vac that names its blower function and ships with attachments.
products.description:
The DXV09PA is a 9 gallon heavy-duty wet-dry vacuum rated at 5 peak HP, sold with attachments and an explicit blower function in the listing. Expect to pay $100 to $200, and it is aimed at contractors and frequent heavy use.

It takes first place because it is the only product here that states the blower function in the name. A named blower mode means the maker designed the exhaust port for it, rather than leaving you to reroute a hose and hope. The 9 gallon tank also copes with sawdust or a flooded basement longer than a 4 gallon unit. Against the DXV04T, you gain capacity and a bigger set of tools, but you give up the lighter, easier-to-carry body.

Buy it if you use a shop vac weekly, or you need to clear a driveway, deck or workshop quickly. It is bulky for stairs, so skip it if you keep your vacuum in a closet.
products.idealFor: Contractors and homeowners who use a shop vac weekly.
products.skipIf: Storage space is tight or you vacuum only occasionally.

products.name: DEWALT DXV04T 4 Gallon 5 Peak HP Portable Corded Wet/Dry Shop Vacuum
products.verdict: A portable 4 gallon, 5 peak HP corded DEWALT for job sites that need dual-purpose power.
products.description:
The DXV04T is a portable corded wet-dry vacuum with a 4 gallon tank and a 5 peak HP motor. It is positioned toward job sites needing dual-purpose power, and it sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It lands second because it gives you the same motor figure as the 9 gallon model at a smaller size. A 4 gallon tank is easy to carry up a ladder or into a van, and the lower cost makes sense for a tool you toss in a truck. The tradeoff is capacity: wet cleanups and sawdust fill it quickly. The listing does not spell out a blower mode as plainly as the DXV09PA, so confirm the exhaust port before relying on it.

Pick it if you work on small jobs, in cars, or on stairs, and want the DEWALT build. If you need a big wet pickup, step up a size.
products.idealFor: Tradespeople and car owners who need a compact, tough vacuum.
products.skipIf: You need to clear large wet spills or lots of sawdust.

products.name: Stanley - SL18116P Wet/Dry Vacuum, 6 Gallon, 4 Horsepower Black
products.verdict: A 6 gallon, 4 HP Stanley with the strongest blower airflow in the budget bracket.
products.description:
The Stanley SL18116P is a 6 gallon wet-dry vacuum rated at 4 HP, in black. Expect to pay $25 to $50, and it is the pick for buyers who want strong blower airflow without paying DEWALT prices.

It lands third because it offers the best capacity and blower reputation for the money, though the build is lighter than the DEWALTs. Plastic latches, a thinner hose and a basic cord are typical at this price, and you should expect them to wear sooner. The 6 gallon tank is a good size for a garage, where a 4 gallon fills too fast and a 9 gallon is too big.

Buy it if you need a blower for leaves, a patio or a workbench, and you do not want to spend much. For daily professional use, buy the DEWALT.
pros: Strong blower airflow for the price
products.idealFor: Homeowners who want a blower and a vacuum for a garage or patio.
products.skipIf: You will use it on a job site every day.

products.name: Vacmaster Professional VDK811PW 0201 8 Gal Wet/Dry Vac Self-Cleaning Filter
products.verdict: An 8 gallon Vacmaster with a self-cleaning filter, good for fine dust and a workshop.
products.description:
The Vacmaster Professional VDK811PW is an 8 gallon wet-dry vacuum with a self-cleaning filter. Expect to pay $50 to $100, and the listing does not give a horsepower figure.

It lands fourth because the filter is the headline. Fine dust clogs a shop vac filter quickly, and a self-cleaning system lets you shake or pulse debris loose without opening the tank. That matters in a woodworking shop, where drywall dust and sanding dust choke pleated cartridges. The listing is thin on motor and blower details, so confirm the exhaust port, and know that Vacmaster is lesser-known than DEWALT or Stanley.

Choose it for a workshop where dust is the problem. Skip it if blower performance is the main thing, because the listing does not promise it.
products.idealFor: Workshop owners who fight clogged filters with fine dust.
products.skipIf: A confirmed blower port is a must for you.

products.name: Amazon Basics Wet Dry Shop Vacuum Cleaner, 4 Gallon, 3 HP Stainless Steel, Grey/Black
products.verdict: A 4 gallon, 3 HP stainless shop vac for garages, cars and small apartments.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics wet-dry vacuum has a 4 gallon stainless steel tank and a 3 HP rating, in grey and black. Expect to pay $50 to $100, and it suits smaller spaces.

It lands fifth because it is a sensible, plain machine with fewer standout features. A stainless tank resists dents and rust better than a plastic drum, which matters if you use it for water or leave it in a damp garage. A 3 HP rating sits below the DEWALT and Stanley, so it will pull less on heavy debris. The listing does not describe a blower mode in detail.

Buy it for car interiors, small garage cleanups and wet spills in an apartment. Look elsewhere for a serious blower.
products.idealFor: Apartment and car owners who need a small wet-dry vacuum.
products.skipIf: You want to blow leaves or clear a large patio.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMXEVBE17250 2.5 Gallon 2.5 Peak HP Wet Dry Shop Vacuum
products.verdict: A 2.5 gallon, 2.5 peak HP Craftsman, the cheapest way to get blower function.
products.description:
The Craftsman CMXEVBE17250 is a compact 2.5 gallon wet-dry vacuum rated at 2.5 peak HP. Expect to pay $25 to $50, and it is aimed at buyers who want a blower function for less.

It lands sixth because the tank is small and the motor figure is modest. A 2.5 gallon tank is fine for a workbench or a car, and tiring in a garage, where you will empty it after a single dust pass. The small body makes it easy to store on a shelf, which counts for something. Compared with the Stanley, it costs about the same but holds less than half as much.

Buy it for light duty and a cheap blower on a patio or deck. Skip it for flooded floors.
pros: Compact body stores on a shelf
Cheap way to get a blower
products.idealFor: Light-duty users who want a cheap blower for a deck or workbench.
products.skipIf: You need to clear water or large dust loads.

products.name: Armor All AA155 1.5-Gallon 2 Peak HP Portable Wet/Dry Vacuum, Orange
products.verdict: A 1.5 gallon, 2 peak HP portable for car interiors and light first-time use.
products.description:
The Armor All AA155 is a 1.5 gallon portable wet-dry vacuum rated at 2 peak HP, in orange. Expect to pay $25 to $50, and it is aimed at first-time buyers.

It lands last because the tank and motor are the smallest in the group. A 1.5 gallon tank is a car vacuum, not a garage vacuum, and it fills within a few minutes of real cleanup. Its portability and low price make it a fine first shop vac, and a good spare for a vehicle. The listing does not describe blower details.

Buy it for the car and tight spaces. For anything bigger, buy a larger tank.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers who mainly clean a car.
products.skipIf: You want to clean a garage or blow leaves.

whatMatters.detail: A blower function means the exhaust is directed through a hose port, so you can push leaves, dust or water. Peak horsepower is not airflow, and the cubic feet per minute figure is the better measure. Look for the word blower in the listing, and a threaded or snap-on exhaust port.

Tank capacity sets how long you can work before emptying. A 2.5 gallon unit suits a workbench, 4 to 6 gallons suit a garage, and 8 to 9 gallons suit a workshop or a basement spill. Bigger tanks are heavier and harder to store.

Peak horsepower is measured at a motor condition that never occurs in use. It helps compare within a brand, but not across brands. Treat it as a rough guide and pay more attention to hose diameter and water lift.

Dry debris needs a cartridge or paper filter, while wet pickup needs it removed or a foam sleeve fitted. Fine dust clogs filters fast, so a self-cleaning design or a washable filter saves money. Check which filter comes in the box.

A crevice tool, a floor nozzle and a long hose make a shop vac useful. A thin hose limits flow, and a short cord limits reach. Look for included attachments and a hose that reaches your car or stairs.

faq.q: How does the blower function work on a shop vac?
faq.a: The motor exhaust air is routed to a port, and you connect the hose to it. The air pushes leaves, dust or water away. Check the manual for the right port, since connecting the hose to the wrong one can reduce airflow.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with a shop vac filter?
faq.a: Using a dry paper filter for wet pickup. Water ruins it and can clog the motor, so remove the paper filter or fit a foam sleeve before sucking up liquid.

faq.q: Is a 9 gallon vacuum worth it over a 4 gallon?
faq.a: If you tackle big cleanups or sawdust from a workshop, yes. For a car, stairs and small jobs, a 4 gallon unit like the DEWALT DXV04T is lighter and easier to store.

faq.q: How do I set up a shop vac for blowing?
faq.a: Remove the hose from the intake, plug it into the blower port, and attach a narrow nozzle for focus. Wear eye protection, since debris flies, and keep the cord clear of the work area.

faq.q: How do I maintain the filter and tank?
faq.a: Empty the tank after each wet job, rinse the foam sleeve, and tap the cartridge filter clean. Dry everything before storing to prevent mildew, and replace worn filters.

faq.q: Can these vacuums pick up water?
faq.a: Yes, all are wet-dry designs. A stainless tank like the Amazon Basics resists rust, and you should check the float shutoff and remove paper filters first.

finalTake: The DEWALT 9 Gallon DXV09PA is the shop vac to buy if blowing matters, because it names the function and carries the build for hard use. The DXV04T is the compact version, the Stanley 6 Gallon is the budget blower, and the Vacmaster is for workshop dust. Treat peak horsepower as marketing, confirm the exhaust port on the listing, and buy for tank size and filter first.
